title: Isomorphism transfer for a restricted component coproduct
statement: Let X, C_i and Y_i be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], indexed by Fin(n), with morphisms ι_i:C_i→X and ν_i:Y_i→C_i, and let U be an open of X. If Sigma.desc ι restricted to U and each ν_i restricted to ι_i^{-1}(U) are isomorphisms, then Sigma.desc (ν_i ≫ ι_i) restricted to U is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, reduction to a dense disjoint union of components; expanded component-open proof in lem-weil-pbc-dense-open-component-modifications, steps 1-3 (Stacks web text checked)

proof.text: For p = Sigma.desc ι, restrict the coproduct injections to obtain a_i:(ι_i^{-1}U).toScheme → (p^{-1}U).toScheme. Their squares with the open inclusions are pullbacks: the inverse image identity is (Sigma.ι_i ≫ p)^{-1}U = ι_i^{-1}U. Mathlib FinitaryPreExtensive.isUniversal_finiteCoproducts gives a colimiting cofan. Cofan.nonempty_isColimit_iff_isIso_sigmaDesc implies Sigma.desc a is an isomorphism. Apply the same construction to f = Sigma.desc (ν_i ≫ ι_i) to obtain the comparison b.

The coproduct of the given restricted ν_i is an isomorphism by Sigma.map_isIso. Verify Sigma.desc b ≫ (f restricted to U) = Sigma.map (restricted ν_i) ≫ Sigma.desc a ≫ (p restricted to U) on each coproduct summand, then cancel U.ι and simplify restrictions. The right side and Sigma.desc b are isomorphisms, hence so is f restricted to U.
